sections.h2: Where is Greenville, Mississippi, and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Greenville is the county seat of Washington County and the largest city in the Mississippi Delta, with 29,670 residents at the 2020 census. That count made it the ninth most populous city in the state. It sits on the eastern bank of Lake Ferguson, an oxbow lake left behind by an old channel of the Mississippi River.

The city covers about 27.7 square miles, of which roughly 26.9 are land. Its current site is the third one to carry the Greenville name. After Union forces burned the second town during the Vicksburg campaign, residents rebuilt three miles away at the highest point on the Mississippi River between Vicksburg and Memphis.

sections.h2: What does Delta history mean for houses in Greenville?
sections.html:
Greenville grew as a cotton trading center and later became a hub of Delta culture. Several residences and other buildings from the late 1800s and early 1900s are listed on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Gamwyn Park Historic District.

Nelson Street is a historic strip of blues clubs that drew crowds in the 1940s and 1950s, and Southern Whispers Restaurant on Nelson Street was the second site identified on the Mississippi Blues Trail.

For owners, this history shows up in the housing. Older homes can carry aging systems, and houses within a historic district may need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the city before exterior changes. The city's planning page lists that certificate among its forms for properties in the Historic District.

sections.h2: How hot and wet is Greenville, and what does that do to a house?
sections.html:
Greenville has hot summers and mild, damp winters, and the numbers help explain why cooling and drainage are standard repair items. The table uses 1991 to 2020 normals from the Greenville Mid-Delta Airport, as summarized on Wikipedia.

  • The record low is 8 F, so exposed pipes and older plumbing are worth a look before a buyer's inspector does it.

sections.h2: What does Greenville's planning office handle that affects a sale?
sections.html:
The City of Greenville's Planning Department handles zoning, building permits, housing inspection and code enforcement. Its staff list on the city site names a Planning and Zoning Director, a Building Inspector, a Housing Inspector and a Code Enforcement Officer, and the department phone is 662-378-1548.

The city's published permit forms include building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing and gas permits, a fence permit, a sign permit and a Garage, Rummage and Estate Sale Permit. That last one is relevant to heirs clearing a house, since an estate sale on the property needs a permit.

  • Zoning regulations are in Appendix B of the city ordinance.
  • The city has a 20-year strategic plan, and its planning page links to it.
  • Greenville holds a Brownfields Assessment grant to inventory and assess underused or possibly contaminated sites, and the Mississippi Development Authority administers the Mississippi Redevelopment Act incentives for cleanup.

Ask the planning office whether your property or a neighboring site is part of the assessment program. You can start at the city's planning page.

sections.h2: Who works in Greenville, and who buys here?
sections.html:
Transportation and gaming appear throughout Greenville's record. Washington County has owned the Port of Greenville since the 1930s, with a five-member commission providing oversight, according to a state legislative review of the Mississippi ports. Two casinos serve the city, Trop Casino Greenville on Lake Ferguson near downtown and Harlow's Casino Resort west of the city near the Greenville Bridge.

The Greenville Mid Delta Regional Airport lies northeast of downtown in unincorporated Washington County. Wikipedia reports that commercial service there is federally subsidized under the Essential Air Service program and includes nonstop flights to Dallas/Fort Worth and Atlanta.

All of Washington County is in the service area of Mississippi Delta Community College. People relocating for a job, a school or a family move often need a fixed closing date, and that is where an as-is sale can work.

sections.h2: How do Washington County property taxes work for a Greenville seller?
sections.html:
Washington County collects property tax through its elected Tax Collector, and real property taxes are payable by February 1 following the tax year. The county tax collector's page says 1 percent per month interest is due on any unpaid balance after February 1, and that the collector must hold a tax sale once a year for unpaid real estate taxes and special assessments.

The assessor lists and values all real estate in the county, helps homeowners file for homestead exemption, and keeps ownership maps. The assessor's page also links to a tax GIS map, which lets you check how your parcel is drawn. Assessment appeals go to the county Board of Supervisors, normally by the first Monday in August.

The state's homestead rules are strict about tax compliance. The Department of Revenue says a person is not eligible if the owner or spouse failed to follow Mississippi income tax laws, and that vehicles must be tagged where they are domiciled, which for a homestead is the home. Confirm your exemption status before you list.

sections.h2: What are the legal steps to close a Greenville home sale?
sections.html:
A Greenville home sale follows the state's standard steps: disclosure, contract, title work, deed and recording. Under Mississippi Code Section 89-1-503, the written property condition disclosure statement must reach the buyer as soon as practicable before title transfers, and the seller should note compliance on the contract or an addendum.

The deed is recorded with the Washington County Chancery Clerk. Washington County collects the $1.00 archive fee, so the state schedule lists $26.00 for a deed, including indexing for the first five pages, plus $1.00 for each added page. Mississippi formatting rules have applied to recordable instruments since 2009 and 2021 and include a name, address and phone number for the preparer.

  • Confirm all taxes are current so nothing goes to the August tax sale.
  • Check for open code notices with the Planning Department.
  • Locate the recorded deed and any prior mortgage release.
  • Use an attorney or title company, since preparing a deed for a fee is the practice of law in Mississippi.

sections.h2: When does an as-is cash offer suit a Greenville house?
sections.html:
An as-is offer suits a Greenville house when repairs, an estate or a code notice would stretch a conventional sale past the owner's timeline. Cash Home Buyers looks at houses in the condition they are in, including older homes with deferred maintenance, so the owner does not need to finish fixes first.

Even then, compare options: ask what repairs would cost, what a listing would require and how long each path would take. The legal steps stay the same either way.

faqs.q: When are Washington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property taxes are payable by February 1 after the tax year. The Washington County Tax Collector says 1 percent per month interest applies to unpaid balances after that date, and unpaid real estate taxes go to an annual tax sale.

faqs.q: Does Greenville require a permit for an estate sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Planning Department lists a Garage, Rummage and Estate Sale Permit among its forms, so heirs clearing a house should apply before holding a sale. Call 662-378-1548 to confirm current requirements.

faqs.q: Where do I file for homestead exemption in Greenville?
faqs.a: Apply with the Washington County Tax Assessor, whose office helps homeowners file. Mississippi applications are due between January 1 and April 1, and you do not need to reapply each year unless your homestead status changes.

faqs.q: Who can appeal a Washington County assessment?
faqs.a: Any owner who disagrees with an assessment can request a hearing with the county Board of Supervisors. The state says the appeal should be filed by the first Monday in August before the taxes are due.

faqs.q: How is a house deed recorded in Washington County?
faqs.a: The deed is filed with the Washington County Chancery Clerk. The published state schedule lists $26.00 for a deed in counties that collect the archive fee, including Washington County, and each page after the fifth adds $1.00.

faqs.q: Do historic district homes in Greenville need extra approval?
faqs.a: Exterior changes to properties in the Historic District may need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the city. The planning page lists the application among its forms, and the Planning Department can confirm whether your address is covered.
